meta.note: LLM-distilled seed routes — community knowledge synthesised from Strava segments, Reddit threads, run club guides, travel resources and training data. Coordinates are approximate start points; OSM pipeline adds precise geometry.

routes.name: Embarcadero to Crissy Field
routes.best_time: Early morning or evening. Weekday mornings quietest.
routes.safety: Well-lit, heavily used, very safe at any hour.
routes.avoid: Midday weekends — crowded around Pier 39 and Fisherman's Wharf.
routes.post_run_food: Ferry Building Marketplace — Blue Bottle Coffee, Hog Island Oyster
routes.signature: The best flat run in SF. Ferry Building to the Golden Gate Bridge base — the bridge gets closer with every kilometre.
routes.local_tip: Run north so the bridge is always ahead of you, not behind. The Pier 39 section is the only bottleneck — if it's crowded just duck onto the parallel Embarcadero street.
routes.instagram_moment: Crissy Field with the Golden Gate Bridge framed perfectly behind you — km 6.5
routes.historical_hook: The Embarcadero was a 6-lane highway until the 1989 earthquake collapsed the freeway — locals voted not to rebuild it, giving runners the waterfront we have today.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: mixed — tourist near piers, local by Crissy Field
run_club_usage: SF Road Runners Tuesday group starts here

routes.name: Golden Gate Park Big Lap
routes.surface_quality: good — JFK asphalt, MLK some patches
routes.obstacles: none on road; roots on inner trails
routes.lighting: partial — main roads lit, park paths not
routes.safety: Safe. Some dark sections near Stow Lake after sunset.
routes.avoid: Saturday afternoons — narrow paths get congested.
routes.transit_to_start: N Judah Muni to 9th & Irving (5 min walk)
routes.post_run_food: Outerlands on Judah St — legendary brunch. Or Java Beach Cafe.
routes.signature: SF's favourite long run. Every local runner has a GGP lap story.
routes.local_tip: Enter at Panhandle for a warm-up flat stretch. The Bison paddock at km 7 is a genuine surprise — there are actual bison.
routes.instagram_moment: Dutch Windmill at the west end — km 8.5, sunrise light is extraordinary
routes.historical_hook: JFK Drive was permanently closed to cars in 2022 after a years-long community campaign — a rare victory for pedestrians over cars in a US city.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: local — this is the runners' and cyclists' park
run_club_usage: SF Road Runners Sunday long run

routes.name: Ocean Beach / Great Highway
routes.surface_quality: good — some sand drift near dunes
routes.best_time: Any time. Sunrise spectacular. Permanently car-free.
routes.best_season: spring, autumn — summer fog can be thick
routes.safety: Very safe. Wind can be strong — run into wind first.
routes.avoid: Peak fog days — visibility drops, cold and damp.
routes.best_use: easy long run, mental reset run
routes.transit_to_start: N Judah to Judah & La Playa (3 min walk)
routes.post_run_food: Java Beach Cafe, Riptide bar (dog friendly)
routes.signature: Fog rolling in off the Pacific as you run south. The most SF thing you can do.
routes.local_tip: Wind almost always blows south-to-north in SF. Run south first into the wind, return with it at your back.
routes.instagram_moment: Looking north at dawn — the fog layer sits perfectly at the cliff line and the windmills emerge from it
routes.historical_hook: The Great Highway was one of the first paved roads in California (1917). San Francisco permanently closed it to cars in 2022, making it a 8km unbroken car-free corridor.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: local — surfers, dog walkers, neighbourhood regulars

routes.name: Batteries to Bluffs (Presidio)
routes.best_time: Morning — trail gets busy later. Not lit.
routes.safety: Safe daytime. No lighting — avoid after dark. Narrow in sections.
routes.avoid: Wet conditions — mud and slip risk.
routes.transit_to_start: Presidio shuttle or 43 bus to Letterman
routes.post_run_food: Presidio Picnic area, or Arguello Market nearby
routes.signature: One of the most beautiful urban trail runs in the world. Period.
routes.local_tip: Start from Baker Beach end and run east — you finish near the bridge overlook with the best views at the end when you're tired.
routes.instagram_moment: Battery Godfrey overlook — bridge perfectly framed, Marin headlands behind
routes.historical_hook: The batteries are WWII-era concrete gun emplacements that watched for Japanese submarines. They were never fired in anger.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: local runner / hiker — no tourists this far off the path

routes.name: Crissy Field to Baker Beach
routes.gradient_character: flat coastal then short climb to Baker
routes.surface_quality: good paved path then gravel trail
routes.shade: minimal on Crissy, partial trees near Baker
routes.best_time: Morning. Crissy Field afternoon wind is brutal.
routes.lighting: partial — Crissy lit, Baker Beach not
routes.safety: Very safe. Popular with families and dog walkers.
routes.avoid: Nothing specific — one of SF's most forgiving routes.
routes.post_run_food: Arguello Market, or coffee at Presidio Social Club
routes.signature: Golden Gate Bridge close enough to touch. Kite surfers over the lagoon.
routes.local_tip: Walk out onto Baker Beach itself — the bridge from sea level is a completely different view to any photo you've seen.
routes.instagram_moment: Baker Beach looking north — bridge towers directly above you
routes.historical_hook: Crissy Field was a military airfield until 1936. The wetlands restoration completed in 2001 is one of the most successful urban ecological restoration projects in the US.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: local/tourist mix — Crissy is known, Baker Beach feels discovered

routes.name: Bernal Heights Loop
routes.gradient_character: steep climb, moderate ridge, steep descent
routes.surface_quality: dirt and grass — can be muddy
routes.best_time: Any time. Sunrise and sunset equally good.
routes.safety: Safe and well-used. Off-leash dogs everywhere — be aware.
routes.avoid: Rain — muddy and slippery. After dark — no lighting.
routes.best_use: hill training, intervals, quick views run
routes.post_run_food: Precita Park Cafe, La Lengua, many Bernal brunch spots
routes.signature: Best bang-for-buck hill training in SF. Views of the entire Bay in every direction.
routes.local_tip: Start from Folsom St side for the steepest approach — then the summit feels earned. The off-leash dog culture at the top is very Bernal.
routes.instagram_moment: Summit at golden hour — entire SF skyline, Bay Bridge, and Mt Tam all visible
routes.historical_hook: Bernal Hill has an unofficial 'Dogpatch community antenna' — locals have decorated the hilltop communication tower for decades. City tried to remove it in 2019; the neighbourhood fought back.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: deeply local — Bernal is one of SF's most community-oriented neighbourhoods

routes.name: Glen Canyon to Twin Peaks
routes.gradient_character: canyon floor flat, then steep sustained climb to Twin Peaks
routes.surface_quality: dirt canyon, paved roads on Twin Peaks
routes.width: narrow trail in canyon, road on Twin Peaks
routes.shade: good shade in canyon, fully exposed on Twin Peaks
routes.obstacles: creek crossings in Glen Canyon after rain
routes.best_time: Morning. Twin Peaks is very exposed — fog and wind can be brutal midday.
routes.lighting: none on canyon or Twin Peaks
routes.safety: Glen Canyon trail can be isolated. Run with a partner early/late.
routes.avoid: Wet season — creek crossings difficult. After dark — no lighting.
routes.transit_to_start: K Ingleside Muni to Diamond Heights (5 min walk)
routes.post_run_food: Diamond Heights Shopping Center — basic options, or Noe Valley cafes
routes.signature: You forget you're in a city inside Glen Canyon. Then you summit Twin Peaks and the whole city is beneath you.
routes.local_tip: The canyon trail is genuinely easy to miss — enter via the Elk St path, not the main park entrance. It's a proper wilderness trail 5 minutes from downtown.
routes.instagram_moment: Twin Peaks summit — SF's most famous panoramic view, entire Bay visible on clear days
routes.historical_hook: Twin Peaks was known as 'Eureka' and 'Noe' by early settlers. The Ohlone people called them 'Los Pechos de la Chola' (the Breasts of the Indian Maiden) — an early Spanish colonial renaming that stuck for decades.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: local — Glen Canyon is a genuine neighbourhood secret

routes.name: Lands End Trail
routes.gradient_character: rolling coastal bluff — constant moderate undulation
routes.surface_quality: compacted dirt, some loose gravel and roots
routes.width: narrow to medium — single file in places
routes.best_time: Low tide morning — more of the coastline visible.
routes.safety: Some sections close to cliff edges — stay on marked trail. Not lit.
routes.transit_to_start: 5 Fulton or 18 46th Ave bus to Merrie Way
routes.post_run_food: Louis' Restaurant on the cliff — oldest restaurant in SF with insane views
routes.signature: Raw, wild, feels nothing like a city. The Sutro Baths ruins are an unreal finish.
routes.local_tip: Check the tide chart before going — at low tide you can scramble down to see the labyrinth on the rocks and the hidden cove below the Baths.
routes.instagram_moment: Sutro Baths ruins at sunset — massive Victorian pools crumbling into the Pacific
routes.historical_hook: The Sutro Baths were the world's largest indoor swimming pool complex when built in 1896 — six pools holding 1.7 million gallons of seawater, seating 3,500 spectators. Burned down in 1966 while being demolished.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: local — Richmond district residents treat this as their backyard

routes.name: Marine Drive Full Loop
routes.surface_quality: some broken/sunken tiles mid-2025 — BMC repairs ongoing
routes.best_time: 5:00–7:30 AM. Pre-sunrise magical — city lights on the bay curve.
routes.best_season: October to March (pre-monsoon heat gets intense April onwards)
routes.safety: Very safe. Police present. Gets crowded by 7am.
routes.avoid: Post 9am — tourist crowds make running impractical. Monsoon — waves can splash promenade.
routes.heat_warning: High — zero shade, gets very hot by 8am in summer
routes.post_run_food: K Rustom ice cream (Churchgate), Kyani & Co (iconic Irani cafe, 10 min walk)
routes.signature: The most iconic run in India. Every serious Mumbai runner has done this. The Queen's Necklace at sunrise is unforgettable.
routes.local_tip: Start at Nariman Point and run north — the curve of the necklace unfolds in front of you. Finish at Chowpatty and get a bhel puri from the beach stalls.
routes.instagram_moment: Nariman Point looking north at 5:45am — the entire necklace curve lit up, city skyline behind
routes.historical_hook: Marine Drive was built on reclaimed land in 1940. The name 'Queen's Necklace' was coined by Air India pilots who could see the arc of streetlights from the air at night.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: mixed — office workers, tourists, runners, very social
routes.event_association: Tata Mumbai Marathon (race course runs here)

routes.name: Carter Road to Bandstand Loop
routes.shade: minimal on sea-facing side, some tree cover inland
routes.best_time: 5:30–7:30 AM. After 8am it gets very crowded.
routes.avoid: Post 8am crowds. Monsoon — waves can splash sections.
routes.best_use: easy run, social run, morning ritual
routes.heat_warning: Moderate — sea breeze helps but summer mornings still warm
routes.transit_to_start: Bandra station (15 min walk) or auto-rickshaw
routes.post_run_food: SodaBottleOpenerWala (Carter Road), Candies Bandra, many cafes on Hill Road
routes.signature: Sea Link views at Bandstand. The old Portuguese fort. The best stretch of running in Bandra.
routes.local_tip: The stretch between Carter Road and Chimbai village (km 2) is the most local, least touristy part — fishermen drying nets on the rocks at dawn.
routes.instagram_moment: Bandstand looking north at the Bandra-Worli Sea Link — best at sunrise when the cables catch the light
routes.historical_hook: Bandra Fort (Castella de Aguada) was built by the Portuguese in 1640 to watch for Dutch and Mughal threats. The ruins at the Bandstand end are one of Mumbai's oldest surviving structures.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: local — Bandra is Mumbai's most cosmopolitan neighbourhood, loved by runners

routes.name: Mumbai Coastal Road Promenade
routes.surface_quality: excellent — brand new as of August 2025
routes.width: very wide — dedicated running and cycling lane
routes.avoid: Peak monsoon — coastal road exposed to heavy swells.
routes.best_use: long run, tempo, best surface in Mumbai
routes.transit_to_start: Uber to Worli Sea Face near Sea Link
routes.post_run_food: Worli Village seafood, Haji Ali area cafes
routes.signature: The future of running in Mumbai. Longer and smoother than Marine Drive. Will become the #1 run in the city.
routes.local_tip: South section from Worli toward Haji Ali — for the north stretch to Bandra, use Bandra–Worli Coastal. Most Mumbaikars still don't know this promenade exists.
routes.instagram_moment: Looking south from Worli end — new bridge infrastructure + sea + city skyline all in frame
routes.historical_hook: The Coastal Road project was one of the most controversial infrastructure projects in Mumbai — activists argued it destroyed fishing community access. It opened August 2025 after years of delays and court battles.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: emerging — the promenade is drawing a new running crowd
routes.poi_density: low — very new, stories still forming

routes.name: Danda to Versova Beach Walk
routes.surface_quality: hard sand at waterline at low tide, very soft above
routes.obstacles: fishing boats, VBSL construction debris at northern end
routes.best_time: Very early morning at low tide — 5:00–6:30 AM.
routes.safety: Safe early morning. Deserted after dark — avoid then.
routes.avoid: High tide — beach disappears. Monsoon — dangerous surf. After dark.
routes.heat_warning: High — zero shade, beach heat intense by 8am
routes.transit_to_start: Andheri station then auto to Juhu Beach
routes.post_run_food: Juhu Beach bhel puri stalls, Prithvi Cafe (Juhu)
routes.signature: Three Bollywood film locations in one run. Fishermen launching boats at dawn. Raw, unfiltered Mumbai.
routes.local_tip: Run at the water's edge — the sand is hardest there and the going is much easier. The fishing boats launching at dawn around 5:30am is something you won't see anywhere else.
routes.instagram_moment: Juhu Beach at sunrise — fishing boats silhouetted against the pink sky, skyline behind
routes.historical_hook: Juhu Beach was where India's first commercial aircraft landed in 1928. The Tata Air Mail service used it as a runway before airports were built.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: mixed — Bollywood adjacent, fishing community, local families

routes.name: Powai Lake Loop
routes.surface_quality: good road surface, dedicated running path in Hiranandani section
routes.shade: good — tree cover on IIT side
routes.obstacles: traffic on road sections near IIT gates
routes.lighting: partial — Hiranandani section lit, IIT side less so
routes.safety: Safe. Good mix of people. IIT campus has security.
routes.heat_warning: Low — shade and lake breeze help significantly
routes.transit_to_start: Kanjurmarg station (15 min auto) or Andheri station
routes.post_run_food: Hiranandani — many cafes and restaurants in the colony
routes.signature: Completely different energy from coastal runs. Green, calm, almost feels like a hill station.
routes.local_tip: Enter via the IIT Bombay campus if you can (open to public in mornings) — the campus road adds a beautiful shaded section that most people miss.
routes.instagram_moment: Lake view from the Hiranandani promenade — flamingos visit the lake in winter mornings
routes.historical_hook: Powai Lake was created artificially in 1891 by the British to supply water to Mumbai. IIT Bombay was founded on its banks in 1958 on what was wilderness — flamingos still come.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: suburban — educated, international crowd from IIT and Hiranandani

routes.name: Shivaji Park Circuit
routes.shade: partial — some trees on north side
routes.obstacles: cricket practice areas, shared with walkers
routes.best_time: 5:00–6:00 AM for space, or 8:30 AM+ when crowds thin.
routes.avoid: 6:30–8:00 AM — shared with hundreds of walkers and cricketers.
routes.best_use: interval training, easy loops, social run
routes.post_run_food: Prakash Shakahari Upahargriha (famous Maharashtrian breakfast), Cafe Mysore
routes.signature: Mumbai's original public fitness ground. The morning crowd is an institution — every age, every level.
routes.local_tip: The early morning crowd (5–6am) includes retired cricketers who trained here alongside Sachin Tendulkar. They are happy to talk.
routes.instagram_moment: The park at 5:30am — dozens of silhouettes doing morning exercise against the dawn light
routes.historical_hook: Sachin Tendulkar practised cricket here in the 1980s under coach Ramakant Achrekar. The park is sacred ground to Mumbai's cricket community.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: deeply local — Dadar is one of Mumbai's most Maharashtrian neighbourhoods

routes.name: Worli Seaface
routes.best_time: Early morning. Can extend into Marine Drive for a longer run.
routes.transit_to_start: Lower Parel station (15 min walk) or auto
routes.post_run_food: Worli Village restaurants, Cafe Noorani nearby
routes.signature: Quieter version of Marine Drive. Worli fishing village on one side, open sea on the other.
routes.local_tip: The Worli fishing village at the south end is one of the oldest koliwada (fishing community settlements) in Mumbai — nets drying at dawn are a window into pre-city Mumbai.
routes.instagram_moment: Sea Link from Worli end at golden hour — the cables are backlit by the setting sun
routes.historical_hook: Worli Koliwada is one of Mumbai's original fishing settlements, predating the city. The Koli people were Mumbai's original inhabitants — their name is the root of 'Koli' which became 'Colaba' in the south.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: local — less tourist than Marine Drive, more authentic

routes.name: Priyadarshini Park Loop (Malabar Hill)
routes.safety: Very safe. Gated park with security.
routes.avoid: Peak evening hours — too crowded for running pace.
routes.heat_warning: Low — shade and Malabar Hill elevation help
routes.transit_to_start: Marine Lines station (20 min walk up Malabar Hill)
routes.post_run_food: Hanging Gardens area snacks, or down into Marine Drive cafes
routes.signature: Hidden gem. Sea views over Marine Drive from a hilltop park.
routes.local_tip: The park is adjacent to the Hanging Gardens and the Towers of Silence (Parsi community). The juxtaposition of this peaceful green hilltop with the sea below is unique in Mumbai.
routes.instagram_moment: Park bench viewpoint looking south over Marine Drive and the sea — entire Queen's Necklace visible
routes.historical_hook: Malabar Hill is Mumbai's most exclusive residential area — home to the Chief Minister's residence and many industrialist families. The Towers of Silence nearby are where the Parsi community performs sky burials.
routes.neighbourhood_vibe: elite residential — quiet, private, very different from the rest of Mumbai

routes.name: Bandra–Worli Coastal Promenade
routes.signature: The full car-free waterfront from Worli Sea Link to Bandra — what runners wanted for years.

routes.name: Juhu Beach
routes.surface_quality: hard sand at waterline at low tide; soft higher on beach
routes.transit_to_start: Andheri or Vile Parle station + auto
routes.post_run_food: Juhu bhel puri stalls, Prithvi Cafe
routes.signature: Classic dawn sand run — Bollywood beach before the crowds.
routes.local_tip: Run at the water's edge at low tide. Avoid monsoon surf and after dark.
routes.historical_hook: Site of India's first commercial aircraft landing in 1928 (Tata Air Mail).

routes.name: Mahalaxmi Race Course
routes.surface_quality: turf club track — soft after rain
routes.signature: Unique 2.2 km dirt oval open to joggers — horses on the infield.
